payload.feature:
Decision 0036 is accepted (ruled 2026-09-03; docs/decisions/0036-egress-is-a-property-of-the-route.md). Enact it. Read the decision first: each of its five rulings names an enforcement binding, and those bindings are this commission — nothing beyond them.

What to build:

1. An `EgressClass` enum — local, contracted, uncontracted — in brokkr-runtime::agents beside TrustTier (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/agents.rs), parsed in agents::load with the same closed-vocabulary refusal naming the file and the key, defaulting to uncontracted on absence (ruling 1). The vocabulary is the engine's; which route belongs to which class is operator data.

2. `Adapter` gains `routes: Map<String, EgressClass>` and agents::load gains a route resolver (ruling 2): a concrete model id of the form <route>/<model> resolves to that route's declared class; an id with no prefix resolves to the adapter's own declared class and no better; an adapter fronting a single destination declares one class at the adapter and no routes. Driver conformance tests cover the prefixed, unprefixed and undeclared-route cases, and the unprefixed case asserts it does not inherit a better class than the adapter's own.

3. Local is structural (ruling 3): the gate-seat refusal in crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle.rs (today at line 1056) keeps reading trust_tier alone. A test seats a local, untrusted route at a gate and asserts the refusal is unchanged.

4. Secret bindings key off the class (ruling 4). A seat declaring bindings (decision 0012) compile-refuses unless its resolved route's class meets a minimum the operator rules into the bundle — a plainly named bundle-level key whose default is contracted, so every bundle on disk keeps its present behaviour. `binding_grant` is superseded: a true grant reads as contracted, a false or absent grant as uncontracted, and the old key stays readable one release so no adapter file is forced to change. Rewrite the existing 0021 ruling 4 compile refusal against the class comparison, keep its fail-closed tests, and add a migration test asserting the five adapters as they stand (claude, codex, dsh, exec, lanetally) resolve to exactly the clearances they have now. Assign no route to a class in adapter data: spark is not ruled local by this slice, and dsh's routes map, if you add the key at all, carries only values that leave every route where it stands.

5. `brokkr doctor` reports, per route, when a declared credential variable is satisfied from the process environment rather than the bindings store, named as a warn by route name (ruling 5). The ambient channel is not forbidden; it stops being invisible.

Do not touch: the wire protocol (egress is compile-time policy and never reaches forge-driver/v1), any journal row, the tier vocabulary, or decision 0021 rulings 2, 3 and 7. Bundle digests move only where a route class is declared — with no route declared, the witness pins in crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/witness_digests.rs and crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/compose_tests.rs should not move; if one does, name the reason in the commit. Full gate as the verify seat knows it, exact coverage included; every new refusal has a test that trips it.

RESIDUAL FINDINGS, not fixed:

[medium, SECURITY] agents/load.rs resolve_route: a model id whose prefix the adapter does NOT name resolves to the adapter's own class rather than to uncontracted. Ruling 1 says "uncontracted is everything else, and is the value of an absent declaration", and an undeclared route is an absent declaration; unlike the unprefixed case (where the id genuinely does reach the adapter's own default destination, which is ruling 2's stated rationale) a prefixed-but-undeclared id names a destination the machine positively knows is NOT the adapter's own. Failure scenario: the operator declares dsh `egress: "contracted"` (having ruled DeepSeek's default route acceptable) and `routes: {"spark": "local"}`; `dashscope/qwen3.8-max` — Alibaba, never ruled — then resolves contracted, clears the default egress_minimum, and a seat may bind a secret toward it. That is the fail-open the decision's own rejected alternative 1 exists to prevent ("granting dsh the binding grant clears the Alibaba and DeepSeek routes at the same stroke"). NOT exploitable on today's data: dsh, codex and lanetally are uncontracted, and claude/exec declare no routes. The behaviour is deliberate, documented in the commit message, and pinned by a test (an_agent_chains_route_resolves_through_the_adapter_that_maps_it exercises exactly this path with a contracted adapter), and the task framing permitted a documented alternative reading — so this is a policy reading for the table, not a fix a review seat should flip.

[info] bundle.rs pinned_model only recognises a literal `--model`/`--model=` at an inline site; anything else (an ambiguous double pin, a provider whose flag differs) yields "" and so resolves to the adapter's own class. Harmless today because 0031's pin requirement refuses such a bundle anyway — but enforce_model_policy runs BEFORE enforce_model_pins in the same compile, so the egress check passes on the wrong destination first and the two rulings are now coupled: relaxing 0031's pin rule would silently widen this one.

[info] `routes` and `credentials` keys are validated against the name grammar but never against the adapter's own model-id prefixes, which are in the same file. A misspelled `routes: {"sparc": "local"}` is a silent dead declaration leaving spark/* at the adapter's class (fail-closed, but silent, against this loader's own stated "a misspelled class must never read as uncontracted by accident" idiom), and a misspelled credentials key produces a doctor warn naming a route that does not exist.

[info] recipes/wager-harness/README.md:88 still explains the mechanism as "binding_grant stays false". I fixed it, found that it moves the wager-harness manifest digest and trips witness_digests.rs, and reverted — a prose sweep inside a witnessed bundle directory needs its own commit with the digest move named, which is not this slice's commission. Flagged so it is not lost.

THE FIX. agents::load::resolve_route read a model id whose prefix the adapter does NOT declare as the adapter's own class. That is the fail-open decision 0036's first rejected alternative exists to prevent: ruling dsh contracted for the DeepSeek route it declares would clear dashscope/* — Alibaba, never ruled — at the same stroke, now through the routes map instead of the old boolean. Ruling 1 says uncontracted is 'everything else, and is the value of an absent declaration', and an adapter silent about a route has made an absent declaration about it. The task framing named this the strong default for case (c). resolve_route now separates three cases: prefixed-and-declared → the route's own class; prefixed-and-undeclared → uncontracted; unprefixed → the adapter's own class and no better (unchanged). The asymmetry between the last two is deliberate and documented at the resolver: an unprefixed id genuinely arrives at the adapter's own destination, which is what the adapter's egress is the operator's word about; a prefixed one names a destination the machine positively knows is not it.

TESTS. Every pre-existing fixture declared an UNCONTRACTED adapter, where the old and new readings agree on the floor — which is why the fail-open was invisible. THREE RESIDUALS, none fixed (see per-finding reason):

1. LOW / SECURITY -- a non-concrete --model pin reads as unprefixed, and so inherits the adapter's own class instead of the floor. bundle.rs:1097 feeds pinned_model(raw).unwrap_or_default() into resolve_route, so "" (no split_once('/')) returns adapter.egress. pinned_model returns None not only when there is no pin but when the pin FAILS concrete(): a character outside [A-Za-z0-9._:/-] (e.g. an Ollama 'model@sha256:...' tag), a value over 80 chars (a Bedrock inference-profile ARN is ~100), or a duplicated --model. For the four built-ins (claude|lanetally|codex|dsh) enforce_model_pins refuses first on the same predicate, so this is unreachable there -- including for dsh, which is the decision's motivating binary. It is reachable for any adapter an operator ADDS, since built_in_model_driver hard-codes that list: an added adapter declaring egress contracted-or-better, with a seat declaring secrets and pinning e.g. '--model partner/qwen@2024', binds the secret on the adapter's own class while actually egressing to route 'partner'. That is a fail-open on the axis ruling 4 exists to fail closed. Not triggerable on this tree (no non-built-in adapter, no 'egress' key in any shipped adapter), which is why it is low and not medium. Not fixed because the repair is a semantic call the operator should make -- distinguishing 'no pin' from 'an unreadable pin' means a new refusal, and the current reading is deliberate and documented in the comment at bundle.rs:1125 (it is what keeps exec, which pins no model at all, at the clearance ruling 4 promises it).

RESIDUAL FINDINGS (none fixed; I changed no file, tree is clean at 2c79b11):

1. MEDIUM / SECURITY — the route resolver never sees a pin written with an adapter's own model_flag. bundle.rs `model_pin` hardcodes "--model" / "--model=", but `model_flag` is per-adapter data (agents.rs:249; fixtures in this very tree use "-m"). For an inline site on an adapter whose flag is not --model, a route-prefixed pin reads as ModelPin::Absent, which resolve_route treats as the unprefixed case and hands the ADAPTER'S OWN class — the exact fail-open the decision's first rejected alternative describes ("a ruling on one destination clears no other the same binary reaches"), reached through a different door than the one commit 4abed63 closed. `enforce_model_pins` does not cover it: built_in_model_driver lists only claude/lanetally/codex/dsh, and this only bites adapters the operator ADDS. Proved, not inferred: I added a throwaway test to model_policy_tests.rs — adapter `many` with egress "contracted", model_flag "-m", and an inline seat `[{brokkr},driver,many,--,-m,elsewhere/large-1]` declaring secrets: ["TOKEN"] — and it COMPILED. (Probe reverted; `git status` clean.) Not a regression — pre-0036 the adapter-level grant cleared every route anyway — but the code comment at bundle.rs claims this case is the only thing standing between an added adapter and its clearance, and for a non---model adapter nothing is. Not fixed here because the fix is policy logic (resolve the adapter before computing the pin and match on its declared flag, leaving command_pins_model on "--model" for the four built-ins) plus its own tests, which is past a reviewer's small-and-safe bar.

2. LOW — doctor's ambient check tests store MEMBERSHIP, not seat binding. report_ambient_credentials skips a route whose variable appears in .forge/secrets.env, but bindings are per-seat declared names resolved by secret::resolve_bindings; a name sitting in the store that no seat declares is never bound to the driver, so if the launching shell exports it the driver still takes it ambiently and doctor says nothing. That is a false negative on exactly the channel ruling 5 exists to make visible.

3. LOW — a route whose prefix is outside the agent-name grammar can never be declared. `routes` and `credentials` keys are checked with valid_name (^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$), but resolve_route splits the concrete model id on the first '/' and `concrete()` admits '.', '_', ':' and uppercase in that prefix. A route like `us.east` or `openai_compat` therefore resolves uncontracted forever with no operator data that can say otherwise. Fail-closed, so not a hole — but it is an unstatable fact, and ruling 1 says class assignment is operator data.

4. INFO — `credentials` is keyed by route only, so an adapter fronting a single destination (four of the five shipped) has no key under which to name its credential variable; ruling 5's warn can never fire for them. Faithful to the ruling's "per route" wording and inert today (no adapter declares credentials), but worth naming as a known edge of the shape chosen.
